title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized String Formatting
description: An unsafe SQL statement is constructed dynamically using direct string concatenation or formatting with user-controlled input, allowing malicious attackers to alter query logic, bypass authentication, or exfiltrate database content.
remediation_steps: Replace string formatting/concatenation with parameterized queries or prepared statements.
Use an Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) like SQLAlchemy or Django ORM.
Implement input validation and strictly type-check parameters before passing to database handlers.
vulnerable_code_example: cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{username}' AND password = '{password}'")
remediated_code_example: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = %s AND password = %s", (username, password))
prevention_best_practices: Never build raw SQL strings from external input.
Enforce least-privilege database user access credentials.
Enable database query logging and anomaly detection.

title: Hardcoded API Key / Secret in Source Code
description: Sensitive credentials such as API keys, passwords, private keys, or tokens are committed directly into source code repositories, exposing credentials to unauthorized parties.
remediation_steps: Immediately revoke, invalidate, and rotate the compromised credential.
Store secrets in environment variables or external secret management systems (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).
Remove secret from git commit history using git-filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner.
prevention_best_practices: Configure pre-commit hooks with Gitleaks or Trufflehog.
Maintain a .gitignore file excluding .env and credential store files.
Use ephemeral, short-lived tokens whenever possible.

title: Command Injection via Unsanitized Subprocess Execution
description: Executing system shell commands with shell=True or passing untrusted strings directly to subprocess calls permits attackers to execute arbitrary system binaries.
remediation_steps: Avoid using shell=True in subprocess module calls.
Pass arguments as a list of strings rather than a concatenated single string shell line.
Use shlex.quote() if system shell evaluation is strictly mandatory.
remediated_code_example:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", user_host], check=True, shell=False)
prevention_best_practices: Avoid invoking OS shell commands whenever native library APIs exist.
Restrict binary execution capabilities via AppArmor / SELinux / Seccomp profiles.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Unescaped user input rendered directly in web pages allows malicious scripts to execute in the victim browser session, compromising cookies, session tokens, or site data.
remediation_steps: Apply contextual output encoding (HTML, JavaScript, URL encoding) on all user-supplied data.
Set Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers restricting inline script execution.
Mark HTTP cookies with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes.
remediated_code_example:
from markupsafe import escape return f"

Welcome {escape(request.args.get('name', ''))}

"
prevention_best_practices: Use auto-escaping web templating engines such as Jinja2 or React.
Enforce strict Content Security Policy headers across web endpoints.

title: Insecure Deserialization via Pickle or Unsafe Loader
description: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle or yaml.unsafe_load allows execution of arbitrary Python objects and shell payloads.
remediation_steps: Avoid Python pickle deserialization for untrusted network payloads.
Use standard JSON, Protocol Buffers, or safe YAML parsers (yaml.safe_load).
Sign and encrypt serialized data payloads using HMAC signatures if pickle is mandatory.
prevention_best_practices: Never accept binary serialized objects directly from external consumers.

title: Root Container Execution in Kubernetes Manifest / Dockerfile
description: Containers running as the root user (UID 0) increase container escape blast radius, exposing the underlying host system to compromise.
remediation_steps: Add a non-root USER directive in Dockerfile.
Specify securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true in Kubernetes Deployment / Pod specs.
Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true in securityContext.
remediated_code_example:
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
RUN useradd -m appuser
USER appuser
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
prevention_best_practices: Enforce Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (Restricted policy).
Scan images in CI pipeline using Trivy or Hadolint.

title: Use of Broken / Weak Cryptographic Hash Algorithm (MD5 / SHA1)
description: MD5 and SHA-1 hashing algorithms are vulnerable to collision attacks and must not be used for secure hashing, signatures, or password verification.
remediation_steps: Upgrade cryptographic hashing algorithms to SHA-256 or SHA-512.
Use argon2, bcrypt, or pbkdf2_hmac for password hashing rather than raw cryptographic hashes.
prevention_best_practices: Enforce TLS 1.3 and modern cipher suites.

title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset Denial of Service Vulnerability
description: Vulnerability in HTTP/2 protocol stream handling allows remote unauthenticated attackers to trigger CPU denial of service via rapid reset requests.
remediation_steps: Upgrade web server/proxy packages (Nginx, Envoy, gRPC, Node.js) to patched versions.
Limit concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection.
prevention_best_practices: Automate dependency vulnerability scanning in CI/CD pipeline.
Apply Dependabot or Renovate bot automated patch management.
